research_question: Does the FORM_SURVIVES_FUNCTION pattern replicate in a second visual tradition when the transmission trace is decomposed into historically separated visual stages rather than only source-versus-modern endpoints?

chosen_trace.object: Paris Danse macabre at the Cemetery of the Saints-Innocents
chosen_trace.role: late-medieval mural baseline / earliest securely attested Parisian visual anchor in this protocol
source_bound_facts: BnF states that the Danse macabre was represented at the Saints-Innocents cemetery in Paris in 1424.
BnF frames the macabre tradition as moral preparation for death and as imagery traversing social ranks.
chosen_trace.function_baseline: moral-didactic memento mori / preparation for death / levelling of social status before death
chosen_trace.caution: Do not reduce the cause to plague alone; late-medieval mortality, war, epidemic, preaching, ars moriendi and broader macabre culture are overlapping context layers.

chosen_trace.object: Hans Holbein the Younger, Dance of Death woodcuts
chosen_trace.role: reproducible print-stage mutation and scale/composition compression
source_bound_facts: British Museum states the series was designed in 1524/25 and cut by Hans Lützelburger before his death in 1526.
British Museum and Metropolitan Museum record publication in Lyon in 1538.
The Met describes scenes in which Death intrudes into daily life and confronts people of differing social roles.
mutation_dimensions: extended social procession -> compact episodic scenes
Death remains active/dynamic while living social agents are interrupted, led, seized or confronted

source_bound_facts: D23 records The Skeleton Dance as the first Silly Symphony released in 1929.
A scholarly Journal of the Royal Musical Association article describes Disney as exploiting the Dance of Death theme in The Skeleton Dance.
mutation_dimensions: static/serial death imagery -> animated synchronized movement
Death-as-social-interrupter motif -> autonomous dancing skeleton ensemble

chosen_trace.object: dark memes / shitposting using dancing skeletons or re-used Dance of Death imagery
chosen_trace.selection_rule: Use dated, sourceable examples and do not count generic skeleton imagery as Danse Macabre descendants without motif or transmission evidence.

core_motifs: dynamic bodily movement associated with dance or forced accompaniment
living counterpart drawn from an identifiable social role or life stage
interaction between Death and the living
baseline_visual_signature.anti_overfit_rule: A skeleton alone is insufficient. At least two high-specificity motifs plus historical or documentary linkage are required for lineage promotion.

lrs_vector.rule: Score each transition independently before computing any endpoint comparison. Preserve uncertainty as intervals rather than false point precision.

A_to_B.question: Which Danse Macabre motifs survive the shift from public mural tradition into Holbein's portable woodcut series?

B_to_C.question: Which high-level Dance of Death motifs survive into The Skeleton Dance, and which are replaced by animation/music/comedy?
B_to_C.firewall: Do not score direct Holbein-specific retention unless a documentary or motif-specific bridge is found.

C_to_D.question: Which dancing-skeleton forms survive into sourceable internet meme families and what happens to mortality/didactic semantics?

A_to_D.question: Endpoint comparison only after intermediate transitions are scored; never substitute endpoint similarity for lineage.

preregistered_hypotheses.H1: Agent/form retention will exceed function-semantic retention across the trace.
preregistered_hypotheses.H2: Gesture/dynamic-movement retention will remain moderate-to-high at family level while specific choreography changes substantially.
preregistered_hypotheses.H3: Affect will shift from moral-serious or threatening toward grotesque/comic/ironic in later popular-media stages.
preregistered_hypotheses.H4: Portable/reproducible media stages will increase copyability, but this protocol does not infer that semantic loss causes transmissibility.

pass_conditions.minimal_pass: A->B and B->C can each be scored with source-bound evidence and at least one high-specificity motif survives while function/affect changes.
pass_conditions.strong_pass: A->B->C->D yields a documented chain where form/agent retention remains consistently higher than function-semantic retention without relying on generic skeleton similarity.
pass_conditions.fail_condition: Modern examples cannot be linked beyond generic skeleton iconography, or the family-level form is not retained more strongly than function after uncertainty is accounted for.

epistemic_firewall: Paris 1424 is a baseline anchor, not automatically the single origin of all later Dance of Death imagery.
Holbein's series belongs to the Dance of Death tradition, but direct copying from the lost Paris mural is not asserted without evidence.
The Skeleton Dance can be treated as a scholarly recognized use of the Dance of Death theme, but direct Holbein-to-Disney transmission remains OPEN.
Generic dancing skeleton memes are not descendants by default.
Plague context is relevant but should not be treated as a monocausal explanation for the medieval tradition.
High formal retention plus low semantic retention does not prove that semantic shedding increases transmissibility.
next_actions: Recover the best available reconstruction/descriptions of the Paris 1424 Saints-Innocents mural sequence and its social-order structure.
Select a fixed subset of Holbein woodcuts with explicit social-role contrasts and dynamic Death interaction for A->B scoring.
Segment The Skeleton Dance into comparable motif units for B->C family-level scoring.
Only then sample dated modern internet examples under a strict lineage/motif rule.
canonical_seal: TRACE THE MUTATIONS THROUGH INTERMEDIATE MEDIA. FORMAL SIMILARITY IS NOT LINEAGE; LINEAGE IS NOT CAUSATION. SCORE EACH TRANSITION BEFORE CLAIMING THAT FORM SURVIVES FUNCTION.
